Spawning Array

Every night at Okinawa from 2020 to 2027, placed by the age of the moon (across, one full turn from one full moon to the next) and by the hours of full dark the night has, with no sun and no moon in the sky (up). The blocks are coloured by day length, so winter and summer nights can be told apart. Pick a species to see its spawning events as filled circles (orange for anemones, teal for corals); other species of the same genus show as squares, and everything else is hidden. “All species” shows every record. Each species keys on its own nights, so compare events within a species and do not pool them. Pick a locale (a group of reef regions tied to our cue sites) to see only the records observed there, with the cue arcs we hold for that locale and the species seen spawning in it.

Recorded spawning events

Coral dates not on the graph

Exact-date coral records from the research hub that cannot be placed on the true sky: tanks with programmed or shifted lights, or sites the source does not name. Three coral records with a real sky are on the graph as squares.

Which moon axis lines the events up?

For each axis, the range the recorded events span and the share of all 2,922 Okinawa nights that fall inside that range. A smaller share means the axis picks out the event nights more tightly. Anemones only: corals are left out because each species keys on its own nights. Six events come from Okinawa itself; the ten-event set adds Wakatobi, Solomons, Ko Phangan and Saipan at their own sites.

Citations

Sources behind the spawning events and coral dates above, numbered in order of first use. Ids on the right are research-hub source ids.

    The small teal dots are the in situ rows of the Indo-Pacific Coral Spawning Database (Baird et al. 2021, 3,569 observations from 1978 to 2019, 275 species). Each dot sits at the record’s own moon age at the site’s sunset and at the hours of full dark that site had that night. Species are not pooled by colour, so hover a dot for its species, site and source.

    The small triangles are records from regions the Indo-Pacific database does not cover, each read from an open source in full: the Flower Garden Banks (northwest Gulf of Mexico) tables of Vize et al. 2005, the Curaçao pillar-coral nights of Marhaver et al. 2015, 143 Maldives Acropora species-nights from the open dataset of Monfared et al. 2023 (colonies on reef frames, pyramids and wild reef, 2021 to 2023), 97 more Maldives species-nights from the 2024 to 2025 colony table of Errington et al. 2025 (28 species, Baa Atoll), seven Florida Keys Acropora palmata nights from Williams et al. 2023, 21 Caribbean Acropora species-nights (Florida Keys, Belize, Panama, 2004 to 2009) from the supplementary table of Fogarty et al. 2012, and one 2024 Red Sea record. They are placed the same way as the dots; hover a triangle for the paper’s own nights-after-full-moon value and the spawning times it reports. Sources that could not be fetched yet are listed in research-hub/library/datasets/atlantic/README.md.
